label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI G4 GST — The Best Part of the Day
text: Mia was in her bedroom when she heard a rooster crow. Then she heard a man yell, 'Hot pandesal! Buy your hot pandesal!' Mia wanted to sleep some more. But she knew she might be late for school if she did. Finally, she began to smell fried eggs and fish. 'It's time to get up,' she said. Mia jumped out of bed and ran down the steps.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI G4 GST — The Philippine Eagle
text: The Philippine Eagle has replaced the maya as our national bird. It is one of the three largest and strongest eagles in the world. But it is in danger of extinction. Hunting and deforestation have caused the number of Philippine Eagles to dwindle. Scientists have tried to increase their number by breeding them in captivity. The first eagle to be bred in captivity is Pag-asa. At 25 years old, Pag-asa is not yet suited to be released to the wild as she has developed dependency on her human keeper.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI G4 GST — Home to Millions of Fish
text: Coral reefs are found in shallow areas of tropical ocean waters. They are like beautiful underwater gardens that grow in salty waters. Millions of fish and sea plants make their home in the reefs as these provide a safe sanctuary for them. They allow small fish to hide from large predator fish. But many coral reefs are in trouble. Water pollution is destroying many reefs. Tourism likewise harms them. If reefs are damaged, we will lose many of our most beautiful fish.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI G5 GST — Early Start
text: Mara woke up very early. She looked at the clock. It said six o'clock. She thought it was a school day, so she got up quickly. She washed her face and brushed her teeth. She put on her school uniform. She went to the kitchen. Her mother looked surprised. 'Why are you dressed so early?' her mother asked. 'It is Saturday,' she said. Mara looked down at her uniform and laughed. She went back to her room and changed into her play clothes.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI G5 GST — The Volcano
text: A volcano is an opening in the earth's surface through which hot liquid rock, ash, and gases escape from below. When a volcano erupts, it can be very dangerous. Lava flows down the sides of the volcano and burns everything in its path. Ash falls like rain and covers the land. People who live near a volcano must be ready to leave quickly when it erupts. Scientists study volcanoes to find ways to warn people before an eruption happens. In the Philippines, Mayon Volcano is known for its almost perfect cone shape.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI G6 GST — Water
text: Water is one of the most important things on earth. All living things need water to survive. People use water for drinking, cooking, and cleaning. Farmers use water to grow crops. Water also helps run machines in factories. The earth has a lot of water, but most of it is salt water found in the oceans. Only a small part is fresh water that people can drink. Rivers, lakes, and underground wells are sources of fresh water. Because clean water is limited, we must be careful not to waste it and not to pollute our water sources.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI G6 GST — Typhoons
text: A typhoon is a strong storm that forms over warm ocean water. It brings heavy rains and very strong winds. Typhoons can cause floods, landslides, and damage to homes and crops. The Philippines is visited by many typhoons each year because it lies in a typhoon belt. When a typhoon comes, people are warned through weather reports on the radio and television. It is important to stay indoors and keep away from flooded areas. After a typhoon, communities come together to help those who were hurt and to clean up the damage.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI G6 GST — Taking Care of Our Eyes
text: Our eyes are very important. We use them to see the world around us. Taking care of our eyes helps us see clearly for a long time. We should read in a well-lit place so our eyes do not get tired. We should sit at a safe distance from the television and computer screen. Eating vegetables like carrots and green leafy foods helps keep our eyes healthy. If your eyes feel tired or you have trouble seeing, you should visit a doctor. Wearing sunglasses outside protects our eyes from too much sunlight.

label: Literal
name: Quezon G7 Intervention — The Legend of Tiaong
text: Once there lived an old and rich woman who lived in a small town in the province of Quezon. She helped people in many ways, because of her kindness, the people in the community learned to love and respect her. Everybody called her "Tia" as a sign of respect. Aside from being kind, she was also religious. When she went to the church to attend the mass, she always rode on her favorite cow. The people got used to seeing her and whenever they heard the sounds made by the cow, they knew that Tia was passing by. Years passed and the people agreed to name their town after her and her cow and so they called their town, "Tia-ong."

label: Literal
name: Quezon G7 Intervention — The Mermaid in Atimonan
text: The story about mermaids, a half-human, and a half-fish creature might seem unrealistic but some believed they exist. In Atimonan, Quezon, they said a mermaid had saved a young fisherman from drowning and was given a magical comb which gave him the power to call the mermaid simply by dipping it into the sea. But a tragic incident happened; the Moro pirates attacked the town; survivors scattered inland towards the safety of the mountains. Nothing was heard of the young fisherman. Years later, locals would claim to see a beautiful maiden sitting on top of the huge boulder by the sea looking at the mountains of Atimonan. However, when they approached her, she jumped into the sea and vanished. Presently, a statue was built on top of the boulder where this maiden was frequently seen.

label: Literal
name: Quezon G7 Intervention — Pagmamano: A Filipino Practice
text: Mano is a Spanish term which means "hand", accompanied by "po" as a means of showing respect to the elders. During the Spanish era, pagmamano was done by kissing the hands of the elders, but as time passed by, it is practiced differently. The elders are the ones putting their hands on the forehead of the children or simply touching their heads. Pagmamano is done by the youngsters as their way of greetings to their parents and to their grandparents. They are seen doing it not just on special occasions like Christmas or New Year or during their family reunions, but almost everyday. This uniquely Filipino-owned practice makes us stand out among other cultures because it mirrors the strong family ties that we have.

label: Literal
name: Quezon G7 Post Test — Cherished Saturday
text: It was Saturday morning. My brother and I woke up very early to attend Thanksgiving Worship Service. We were not used to get up early on Saturdays unless for a very special occasion. Of course, special occasions seldom happen. My family hurriedly prepared because we need to arrive early to the church. Almost all seats in the church were occupied by the brethren when we arrived. Fortunately, there was a deacon who guided us to the reserved seats. Alas, we comfortably sat and do our own devotional prayers to the Lord. Moments later, I felt the peace within my soul as the choir sang the hymn soulfully. Then, the minister began his preaching of God's words. The brethren were all eyes and ears from the beginning till the end of the gospel. Through the gospel, each member of the church was enlightened spiritually. It was Saturday morning, for which I can say was one of the best Saturdays of my life!

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI G7 GST — Telling Time
text: Humans have used different objects to tell time. In the beginning, they used an hourglass. This is a cylindrical glass with a narrow center which allows sand to flow from its upper to its lower portion. Once all the sand has trickled to the lower portion, one knows that an hour has passed. Using the same idea, water clocks were constructed to measure time by having water flow through a narrow passage from one container to another. On the other hand, sundials allowed people to estimate an hour by looking at the position of the shadow cast by the sun on a plate. At night, people measured time by checking the alignment of the stars in the sky. None of these were accurate, though. The clock was the first accurate instrument for telling time.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI G7 GST — Counting the Hours
text: When men decided to divide the day into twenty-four hours, they used numbers one through twelve two times. As a result, there was one o'clock during the day and another one o'clock after midnight. This created confusion. If one was told to submit a project at six o'clock, did this mean six o'clock in the morning or at night? The Romans provided a solution to this problem. They thought that noon time, the time when the sun is at its apex, is an important time. They called noon Meridies and measured time by this. They called the morning ante meridiem, which means 'before noon' while 'after noon' was called post meridiem. Ante meridiem was shortened to A.M. while post meridiem was shortened to P.M.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI G7 GST — Nosebleeds
text: Having a nosebleed is a common occurrence. Children experience epistaxis when blood flows out from either or both nostrils, often for a short period of time. It may be caused by one's behavior like frequent nose picking or blowing too hard when one has a cold. It may also be caused by certain physical factors such as an allergy or abnormal growths in the nasal cavity. Or it may be due to environmental conditions such as exposure to toxic fumes or dryness of the air. While it is often thought that holding one's head back can treat a nosebleed, this can actually cause one to choke or vomit. The best thing to do is to lean forward, pinch the top of the nose and apply a cold compress. And if that doesn't work, it's best to get professional help.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI G7 Pre Test — Dark Chocolate
text: Dark chocolate finds its way into the best ice creams, biscuits and cakes. Although eating chocolate usually comes with a warning that it is fattening, it is also believed by some to have magical and medicinal effects. In fact, cacao trees are sometimes called Theobroma cacao which means 'food of the gods.' Dark chocolate has been found out to be helpful in small quantities. One of its benefits is that it has some of the most important minerals and vitamins that people need. It has antioxidants that help protect the heart. Another important benefit is that the fat content of chocolate does not raise the level of cholesterol in the blood stream. A third benefit is that it helps address respiratory problems. Also, it has been found out to help ease coughs and respiratory concerns. Finally, chocolate increases serotonin levels in the brain. This is what gives us a feeling of well-being.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI G7 Pre Test — Sneezing
text: Sneezing happens when our body is trying to remove an irritation found inside the nose. A special name for this process is sternutation. How does a sneeze happen? When your nose is tickled, the sneeze center in our brain receives a message. Soon, the other parts of the body that work together to create a sneeze such as the abdominal muscles, chest muscles, the diaphragm, the muscles of the vocal chords, the back of the throat, and the eyelids receive this message. An explosion as fast as 161 kilometers per hour sends the irritant speeding out of your nose. Examples of irritants in the air are dust, pepper, or allergens such as pollen. Some experience having a photic reflex and sneeze as soon as they are under the bright sun. Now, if it ever happens that a sneeze of yours gets stuck, look towards a bright light to unstick your stuck sneeze.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI G7 Pre Test — Dust
text: No matter how often we sweep the floor of our homes, we are still able to gather together a considerable amount of dust. Dust is all around us. It gathers on bookshelves, on furniture - old or new. These particles rest on any still object - undisturbed until touched or wiped clean. Dust, which was first believed to be made of dead skin has been found to be a mix of different things. Some of the common ingredients of dust particles include animal fur, dead insects, food, fiber from clothes, beddings, soil and other chemicals. Although most of household dust comes from the outside through doors, windows and shoes, other dust particles come from within. Scientists have discovered that the mix of dust from each household actually depends on four things: the climate, the age of the house, the number of persons who live in it and their individual cooking, cleaning and smoking habits. Making our homes free of dust may not be possible but lessening the amount of dust that we keep in our homes will help avoid possible allergies and allow us to breathe well.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI G7 Pre Test — Pain
text: How do we sense pain? The human body has nociceptors to receive an electrical impulse that is sent to part of the brain that recognizes pain. Memories of these sensations are formed to help us avoid painful objects and experiences and prevents us from repeating past mistakes that may have hurt us in some way. But pain is more complex. It is not only a physical experience but an emotional and psychological one as well. When all of these come together, it is called suffering. The mind is not alone in recognizing pain. The nervous system is also able to store such information. Even when a person loses a finger or a limb, the pain that was once felt may become a chronic one - one that keeps recurring. The best way to avoid this is to prevent pain memories from forming. The use of anesthesia prevents the mind from creating these memories. Drugs that prevent pain such as analgesics help lessen the pain sensed.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 GST — Chami
text: If there is one menu that most people in Lucena would like to order, it's probably their favorite "chami". With only P25.00 to P40.00 per order, one can experience tasting the delectable pancit made from flat or round noodles. In fast food chains or small restaurants, this menu is always on the top list, whether it's ordinary or special. Caldo or chicken broth, when mixed with the ingredients like shrimps, liver, squid balls or fish balls and vegetables makes the chami tastier. Since it's the city folk's favorite, "Lucenahin" include Chami Festival as one of the highlights of the fiesta celebration held during the month of May. People serve as judges in choosing the most delicious chami prepared by different chefs from nearby barangays in Lucena, City.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 GST — Paragos: A Local Color
text: Most of the areas in Quezon are still considered as agricultural. Rice, corn, coconut and other root crops such as camote, cassava and ube are only some of the harvested products in the rural and far-flung barrios in Lucena and Quezon. Since these areas are too far from the city, farmers have a hard time bringing these products in the markets. Paragos (sledge) serves as a mode of transportation of the barrio folk. This can help them transport and sell their goods in the town or city proper. It resembles the physical look of a car. It is the version of the four wheels in the city's concept of limousine. It is made up of wood. It contains pair of palunas (paddle) touching the ground. With the help of a carabao, the paragos is pulled to walk.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 GST — Quezon's Local Hero
text: Every fourth day of November, people in Quezon Province commemorate the death of Hermano Puli. Apolinario Dela Cruz, also known as Hermano Puli was born on July 22, 1814 in Barrio Pandac, still in Quezon Province. He was a charismatic leader whose crusade for religious freedom turned into a major revolt against the Spanish rule in the Philippines in the early 19th century. He put up a religious confraternity called the Cofradia de San Jose. Because of his passionate leadership, he was able to attract hundreds of followers from nearby towns in Tayabas, Laguna and Batangas. The governor general that time discovered that the Cofradia limited its membership to Indios. He ordered Puli's arrest. Puli fled but was captured the next day. He was executed and his body was cut into pieces and his head was hung on a pole.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 Pretest — Bamboo Bridges
text: Consider passing along the roads of Quezon Province, there are many sights to hold you in awe. One may not notice it, but the wonderful one-line bridge made of bamboo trunks connecting the coconut trees is a view one cannot ignore. These bamboo bridges are connected to the uppermost parts of the coconut trees which are more than 20 feet above the ground. They are made delicately and properly in order to make sure that they could support the weight of the tuba makers (mangangarit), who seem fearless while crossing from one bridge to the other while harvesting the tuba (coconut wine) through the use of tukil (bamboo pitcher). Crossing the coconut bridge seems dangerous so they have to be careful because one wrong step may lead to falling; once they fall, one may die or paralyze for life.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 Pretest — Niyogyugan: A Festivity
text: Niyogyugan Festival is one of the famous festivals in Quezon which name derived from the words: niyog (coconut), Quezon's main agricultural products; and yugyugan (to shake or to move). The Quezon provincial government has celebrated the Niyogyugan since 2012, a feast held every August, a thanksgiving for the bountiful harvest of coconut. It aims to unite all the municipalities of the province and to promote the coconut industry as well as the other local delicacies and products. This festival is a week-long festivity which showcases several events such as the Bb. Niyogyugan, which is the highlight of the celebration; Niyogyugan Invest Forum; Niyogyugan Kusineros; Karosa ng Niyog — float competition and a lot more. They also have "Araw ng Pamilyang Magsasaka" recognition for all the farmers in Quezon, and "Teachers' Convention Day" to honour all the teachers in the province.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 Pretest — Lucenahin's Tagalog
text: Philippines has plenty of dialects; Tagalog is just one of those. But many are not aware that even Tagalog, a distinct dialect of its own has many different local versions. One of these is the Tagalog used in Lucena. Lucenahin use Tagalog words that are understood by them but may sound strange for some Tagalog speakers. Someone who is not native in Lucena might hear Lucenahin say words such as dayag which means "washing the dishes" or akit which means "to invite". Halang or mahalang which means "spicy"; and abuhan which means "stove" or maribuso which means "naughty". Abyad which means "to settle or to take care of someone or something" and the likes might raise their eyebrow because it sounds strange than the usual. Lucenahin might speak a different version of Tagalog but it only proves that language is really dynamic.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 Pretest — Manuel L. Quezon Monument
text: In 1946, Godofredo Magallanes promised Quezon's widow, Aurora, that a monument of Quezon would be built as a tribute to his participation and struggle for the Philippine independence from the United States. After 4 years, the plan for building the monument was conceived. Gov. Vicente Constantino appealed to all the residents of Quezon province for the donations through Christmas cards in 1952. Twelve sacks of one centavo coins donated by public elementary students from all over Tayabas Province (now Quezon Province) were collected and shipped to Milan, Italy where it was sculpted by an Italian. The Quezon monument was then erected in 1954 along with the marble wall that contains Pres. Quezon's message to the people, and was inaugurated on August 19, 1955 by Pres. Ramon Magsaysay during the celebration of the 77th birth anniversary of Pres. Manuel L. Quezon.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 Post Test — Bulungan
text: Early at dawn when everyone is sound asleep at around 1 to 2 in the morning, big and small time capitalists, buyers, sellers, middlemen and fishermen gather at the Lucena Dalahican Port for "Bulungan". Bulungan means secret auction, a way of selling and buying raw and fresh sea food products. This secrecy in bidding serves the purpose of buying bulk seafood products at a cheaper cost. How do sellers and buyers transact using this business method? Buyers and sellers alike use a secret code in doing transactions. The seller whispers the price of his seafood products in bulk using a code. Prudence must be exercised both by the seller and buyer in bidding for a satisfying return of investment. Odd as it may seem but this practice has been going around for years with an unknown root.

label: Inferential
name: Quezon G7 Post Test — Kiping
text: Kiping, a leaf-shaped decorative piece highlights the Pahiyas Festival in Lucban. How is kiping made? First, it is made from carefully selected leaves used as moulders. The kinds of leaves include kabal, kape, talisay (umbrella tree), kakaw (cocoa), antipolo and banana (saba). The leaves should be matured. They are cut into uniformed sizes. Next is the preparation of rice paste. A C-64 rice variety that has been stocked for a year is soaked in water for two hours before grinding. Then, the grounded rice is mixed with three packets of food color and rock salt. Finally, the paste will be spread on individual leaves and cooked in an improvised steamer made of bamboo slats for 30 minutes. Once dried under the shade, peel off from the mould, place each one on top of the other, compress them for half a day, then store in a clean box or decoratively hang them. The complexity of the process makes Kiping truly a product of art and hardwork.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI G8 — Deforestation and Its Consequences
text: Deforestation refers to the large-scale removal of forests, primarily driven by agricultural expansion, logging, and urban development. When trees are cleared, the ecological balance of an area is profoundly disrupted. Forests serve as carbon sinks, absorbing vast amounts of carbon dioxide that would otherwise contribute to the greenhouse effect and accelerate climate change. The loss of tree cover also destabilizes soil, increasing the risk of erosion and landslides, particularly in mountainous regions. Biodiversity collapses as wildlife lose their natural habitats, pushing numerous species toward extinction. Indigenous communities whose livelihoods depend on forest resources are likewise displaced. Addressing deforestation requires coordinated policy interventions, reforestation programs, and a shift in global consumption patterns that drive demand for forest-derived products.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI G8 — The Water Cycle and Climate Regulation
text: The hydrological cycle is a continuous process by which water circulates through the Earth's systems — from the oceans and land surfaces, through the atmosphere, and back again. Solar energy drives evaporation, lifting water vapor into the atmosphere where it condenses to form clouds. Precipitation then returns water to the surface, replenishing rivers, lakes, and groundwater reserves. This cycle is intimately connected to climate regulation: the evaporation of water absorbs heat, cooling the surface, while condensation releases latent heat in the upper atmosphere. Human activities that alter land cover — such as deforestation and the expansion of impervious urban surfaces — disrupt local precipitation patterns and reduce the land's capacity to absorb and retain water. Understanding these dynamics is critical for managing water resources sustainably in the face of a changing climate.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI G8 — Propaganda and Media Literacy
text: Propaganda is the deliberate use of biased or misleading information to promote a particular agenda or manipulate public opinion. Historically employed by governments during wartime, propaganda has evolved in the digital age into subtler forms that permeate social media, advertising, and political discourse. Techniques include appeal to fear, bandwagon fallacies, cherry-picking evidence, and the use of emotionally charged language designed to bypass rational analysis. Media literacy — the ability to critically evaluate sources, identify logical fallacies, and distinguish fact from opinion — is therefore an essential competency in contemporary civic life. Developing this skill requires not only exposure to diverse viewpoints but also an understanding of the economic and ideological interests that shape the production and dissemination of information.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI G9 — Climate Change and Resilience
text: Climate change poses one of the most complex and far-reaching challenges of the twenty-first century, requiring responses that transcend national boundaries and integrate scientific, economic, and sociopolitical dimensions. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change has documented that global average temperatures have risen by approximately 1.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, driven primarily by anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. The consequences — more frequent extreme weather events, rising sea levels, and shifting agricultural zones — disproportionately affect developing nations and vulnerable communities that have contributed least to the problem. Building resilience necessitates both mitigation strategies, such as transitioning to renewable energy, and adaptation measures, including climate-proofing infrastructure and diversifying food systems. The principle of common but differentiated responsibilities underscores that while all nations must act, wealthier countries bear a greater obligation to lead and to finance global solutions.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI G9 — The Philosophy of Justice
text: Justice is a foundational concept in moral and political philosophy, yet its precise meaning remains contested across theoretical traditions. Distributive justice concerns the fair allocation of resources, opportunities, and burdens within society. John Rawls, in his influential work A Theory of Justice, proposed that just arrangements are those that rational individuals would choose behind a 'veil of ignorance' — that is, without knowledge of their own social position, talents, or circumstances. This thought experiment yields two principles: equal basic liberties for all, and inequalities permitted only insofar as they benefit the least advantaged members of society. Retributive justice, by contrast, focuses on proportionate responses to wrongdoing, while restorative justice prioritizes the repair of harm and the rehabilitation of offenders. Each framework reflects different assumptions about human dignity, social obligation, and the purpose of law.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI G10 — Colonialism and National Identity
text: The legacies of colonialism continue to shape the political, economic, and cultural landscapes of formerly colonized nations long after formal independence. Colonizers systematically dismantled indigenous institutions, imposed foreign languages and religions, and restructured economies to serve metropolitan interests rather than local needs. The psychological dimensions of this process — internalized inferiority, cultural alienation, and the devaluation of indigenous knowledge — were analyzed by theorists such as Frantz Fanon and Jose Rizal, who argued that decolonization requires not only political liberation but also a profound reconstitution of collective identity. In the Philippine context, the struggle to define a coherent national identity has involved negotiating multiple layers of Spanish and American colonial influence alongside a rich and diverse archipelagic heritage. Contemporary debates around language policy, historical memory, and cultural production reflect the ongoing work of this decolonial project.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI G10 — Globalization and Cultural Homogenization
text: Globalization — the accelerating integration of economies, cultures, and information systems across national boundaries — has generated profound debate about its effects on cultural diversity. Proponents argue that global connectivity fosters intercultural understanding, expands access to ideas and technologies, and creates new hybrid cultural forms that enrich the human experience. Critics, however, warn of cultural homogenization: the dominance of Western, particularly American, media and consumer culture threatens to erode local languages, traditions, and value systems. The concept of 'glocalization' attempts to capture the more nuanced reality in which global influences are filtered through and adapted to local contexts, producing neither pure uniformity nor unchanged tradition. The challenge for societies in an interconnected world is to participate in global exchange while cultivating the critical awareness needed to preserve and revitalize what is distinctive and irreplaceable in their own cultural heritage.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI G10 — Artificial Intelligence and Ethics
text: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly embedded in consequential decisions affecting employment, healthcare, criminal justice, and national security. As these systems grow in sophistication and autonomy, they raise profound ethical questions that existing legal and regulatory frameworks were not designed to address. Algorithmic bias — the tendency of machine learning models to replicate and amplify the prejudices present in their training data — has produced documented disparities in facial recognition accuracy across racial groups and in recidivism risk scores used in sentencing. Transparency and explainability present further challenges: many high-performing models operate as 'black boxes' whose internal logic cannot be readily inspected or contested by those affected by their outputs. Meaningful governance of AI requires interdisciplinary collaboration among technologists, ethicists, legal scholars, and affected communities to establish accountability mechanisms that keep these powerful tools aligned with human values and rights.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Pre G4 — Anansi's Web
text: Anansi is a spider who appears in African folktales. He is known for being clever and tricky. One day, Anansi heard that all the stories in the world belonged to the Sky God, Nyame. Anansi wanted to have these stories. He climbed up to the sky to ask Nyame for them. The Sky God laughed. He said that many great warriors had tried but no one could pay the price. Anansi asked what the price was. Nyame said he must bring Onini the Python, Osebo the Leopard, and a swarm of bees. Anansi went home and thought of a plan. He was clever enough to use his web to catch all three. He brought them to the Sky God. Nyame was so amazed that he gave Anansi all the stories. From that day on, all stories are called Spider Stories.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Pre G5 — Amy's Good Deed
text: Amy was walking home from school one afternoon when she noticed an old woman trying to cross a busy street. The old woman looked confused and afraid. Cars were moving fast and no one seemed to care. Amy put down her bag and walked over to her. 'May I help you cross the street?' she asked. The old woman smiled gratefully. 'Yes, please,' she said. Amy held her hand and waited for the light to turn green. Carefully, she guided the old woman to the other side. 'Thank you, my dear,' the old woman said warmly. 'You are very kind.' Amy smiled and continued on her way home. That night, she told her mother what happened. Her mother hugged her and said, 'I am proud of you, Amy. Helping others is one of the best things you can do.'

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Pre G6 — Dreams
text: Everyone has a dream. Some people dream of becoming doctors, teachers, or engineers. Others dream of becoming famous singers or athletes. But a dream is not just a wish. A dream is a goal that you work toward every day. If you want to become a doctor, you must study hard in school. If you want to become a musician, you must practice every day. Dreams give us a reason to get up in the morning. They give us hope when life is hard. Some people say that dreams are for children, but that is not true. People of all ages have dreams. The important thing is to believe in your dream and to take steps toward it. No dream is too small or too big. With hard work, courage, and determination, any dream can come true.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Pre G7 — Lili the Lizard and Koko the Gecko
text: Lili the lizard lived in a sunny patch of rocks near the river. Koko the gecko lived on the cool wall of an old stone house. They were very different from each other, but they were the best of friends. One day, Lili found a large pile of ripe berries under a tree. 'Koko!' she called. 'Come and share these berries with me.' Koko climbed down from the wall. 'But I am afraid of the open ground,' he said. 'The hawk watches from the sky.' Lili thought for a moment. 'Then I will be your lookout,' she said. 'I will watch the sky while you eat.' So Koko went to the berries while Lili kept watch. When she saw a hawk circling, she signaled Koko and they both hid under the rocks. Later, when Lili was cold and could not find warmth, Koko found her a spot on the warm stone wall. They took care of each other because they knew that two friends, even very different ones, are stronger than one.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Pre G8 — The Amazing World of Coral Reefs
text: Coral reefs are sometimes called the 'rainforests of the sea' because they are among the most biologically diverse ecosystems on Earth. Although they cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, coral reefs are home to more than twenty-five percent of all marine species. Corals themselves are not plants but tiny animals called polyps that live in colonies. Over thousands of years, their skeletons accumulate to form the massive structures we see today. These reefs provide critical services: they protect coastlines from erosion caused by waves and storms, support the livelihoods of hundreds of millions of people through fisheries and tourism, and serve as breeding grounds for commercially important fish species. Despite their importance, coral reefs face severe threats from climate change, ocean acidification, pollution, and destructive fishing practices. Rising ocean temperatures cause coral bleaching, a phenomenon in which corals expel the symbiotic algae that give them color and nutrients, leaving them white and weakened. Without urgent action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve local water quality, scientists warn that the majority of the world's coral reefs could be severely degraded within decades.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Pre G9 — Tesla's AI Robot Ready in September
text: Elon Musk announced in August 2023 that Tesla's humanoid robot, named Optimus, would be ready for limited production by September of that year. The robot, which stands approximately 1.7 meters tall, is designed to perform tasks that are dangerous, repetitive, or boring for humans. Optimus uses the same AI technology that powers Tesla's self-driving cars, including cameras and a neural network that allows it to recognize and interact with its environment. In recent demonstrations, the robot was shown sorting objects, carrying boxes, and even performing simple household tasks such as watering plants. Musk stated that Tesla ultimately plans to sell the robot to consumers for less than twenty thousand dollars. However, AI researchers have expressed caution about such projections, noting that the gap between laboratory demonstrations and reliable real-world performance remains significant. The development of humanoid robots raises profound questions not only about technological capability but also about the future of work and the ethical implications of deploying machines that increasingly resemble and interact with humans.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Pre G10 — Butuan Archeological Sites
text: Butuan City in Agusan del Norte, situated in the northeastern portion of Mindanao, holds one of the most significant archaeological records in all of Southeast Asia. For centuries, Butuan was a prosperous trading kingdom whose connections extended to China, India, and other parts of the ancient Malay world. The most celebrated discovery associated with Butuan is the golden artifacts unearthed in the area, including the Golden Tara of Agusan — a seated figure weighing approximately two kilograms of high-carat gold, believed to date from the ninth to tenth century CE. Of equal importance are the balangay, ancient plank boats excavated from the mudflats of Ambangan, which are among the oldest watercraft ever found in Southeast Asia. These vessels provide tangible evidence of the maritime capabilities and trade networks of pre-colonial Philippine societies. The Butuan artifacts challenge the notion that Philippine civilization before Spanish colonization was primitive or isolated, revealing instead a sophisticated polity that was deeply embedded in regional exchange systems. Ongoing excavations continue to yield objects — gold ornaments, Chinese porcelain, and bronze artifacts — that enrich our understanding of a dynamic and cosmopolitan culture that flourished long before European contact.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Post G4 — Marian's Experiment
text: Marian loved science. One afternoon, her teacher asked the class to do an experiment at home. The task was to grow a plant from a seed. Marian chose a bean seed. She planted it in a small pot filled with soil. She placed the pot near the window where it could get sunlight. Every morning, she watered it with just enough water. She wrote down what she observed each day in a small notebook. On the fifth day, she saw a tiny green shoot poking up from the soil. She was so excited that she called her grandmother to come and see. 'You did it!' her grandmother said. By the end of two weeks, Marian had a healthy bean plant with two small leaves. She brought it to school and shared her notes with her class. Her teacher smiled and said it was the most careful experiment in the class.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Post G5 — Trading Places
text: Marco and his older sister Clara never seemed to agree on anything. Marco thought chores were unfair because Clara always got the easier ones. Clara thought Marco was lucky because he did not have to cook. One Saturday, their parents suggested they trade places for the day. Marco had to cook lunch while Clara did the yard work. Marco went to the kitchen and stared at the pots and pans. He did not know where to start. He burned the rice and added too much salt to the soup. Clara, meanwhile, struggled under the hot sun raking leaves and pulling weeds. By noon, they were both exhausted. Over their imperfect lunch, they looked at each other and laughed. 'Your job is harder than I thought,' Marco admitted. 'So is yours,' Clara said. From that day on, they stopped complaining and started helping each other instead.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Post G6 — Flying Rocks
text: On June 15, 1991, Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines erupted in one of the most powerful volcanic explosions of the twentieth century. The eruption sent a column of ash and gases more than thirty-five kilometers into the sky. Rocks and volcanic material were hurled into the air at tremendous speeds. Some fragments, called pyroclasts, traveled hundreds of kilometers from the volcano. The eruption released so much sulfur dioxide that it temporarily lowered global temperatures by about half a degree Celsius. Before the eruption, scientists and government officials successfully evacuated more than fifty thousand people from the surrounding area, saving tens of thousands of lives. The volcanic ash covered farmland, collapsed rooftops, and buried entire villages under meters of lahar — a dangerous mixture of volcanic ash, rock, and water. The Pinatubo eruption demonstrated both the destructive power of nature and the life-saving importance of early warning systems and disaster preparedness.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Post G7 — The Jeepney: A Filipino Tradition
text: The jeepney is one of the most recognizable symbols of the Philippines. Originally made from American military jeeps left behind after World War II, these colorful vehicles were converted by Filipino mechanics and entrepreneurs into passenger transport. Over decades, the jeepney evolved into an art form: each one is uniquely decorated with chrome horses, colorful paintings, religious icons, LED lights, and the names of the driver's family or hometown. For many Filipinos, riding the jeepney is not just a way to get from one place to another — it is a daily ritual that connects them to their neighbors and to their history. However, the traditional jeepney is now threatened. The government's Public Utility Vehicle Modernization Program requires older jeepneys to be replaced with newer, more fuel-efficient models that meet emission standards. Supporters of the program say the modern jeepneys are safer and cleaner. Critics argue that the old jeepneys represent a cultural heritage that should be preserved. The debate over the jeepney's future reflects a wider tension in Philippine society between modernization and the preservation of national identity.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Post G8 — The Impact of Social Media on Communication
text: The rise of social media platforms over the past two decades has fundamentally altered the way human beings communicate. Networks such as Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok have made it possible for individuals to share information instantly with millions of people across the globe, collapsing barriers of time and distance that once defined human interaction. Proponents argue that social media has democratized public discourse, giving ordinary citizens a voice in conversations once dominated by governments and corporations. It has also proven invaluable for organizing social movements, coordinating disaster relief, and maintaining personal relationships across borders. However, critics highlight significant costs. The algorithmic design of social media platforms tends to prioritize emotionally charged content that maximizes engagement, often amplifying misinformation, outrage, and polarization. Research has linked heavy social media use among adolescents to increased rates of anxiety, depression, and poor body image. The ephemeral nature of online communication has also been associated with a decline in the quality of public deliberation, as complex issues are reduced to short posts and reactive comments. Understanding these trade-offs requires not only technological literacy but also a critical awareness of the economic interests that shape the platforms mediating our social lives.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Post G9 — The Rise of AI in Education
text: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into educational systems around the world, raising fundamental questions about the future of teaching and learning. AI-powered tools already personalize instruction by analyzing student performance data and adapting content to individual learning pace and style. Platforms powered by large language models can generate practice problems, explain concepts in multiple ways, and provide instant feedback on student writing — functions previously performed exclusively by human educators. Proponents argue that AI can democratize access to high-quality instruction, particularly in underserved communities where qualified teachers are scarce. In the Philippines, where classroom overcrowding and unequal resource distribution remain persistent challenges, AI-assisted learning holds particular promise. Yet critics warn against uncritical adoption. AI systems trained primarily on English-language data may poorly serve students in multilingual contexts or perpetuate cultural biases embedded in their training corpora. There is also the risk of over-reliance: students who depend on AI for answers may develop shallow understanding rather than the deep critical thinking skills that rigorous education aims to cultivate. The most productive vision of AI in education is not a replacement for teachers but a powerful tool that enables educators to do their jobs more effectively.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS EN Post G10 — Exploring Non-Mendelian Genetics
text: Gregor Mendel's foundational experiments with pea plants in the nineteenth century established the basic principles of hereditary transmission — dominance, recessiveness, and the independent assortment of traits. For nearly a century, the Mendelian framework provided the conceptual backbone of genetics. However, as molecular biology advanced in the twentieth century, it became clear that many traits do not follow Mendel's simple rules. Incomplete dominance occurs when neither allele is fully dominant, producing a phenotype intermediate between the two parental forms. Codominance, observed in human blood type genetics, involves the simultaneous expression of both alleles. Polygenic inheritance, in which multiple genes contribute to a single trait such as height or skin color, produces the continuous variation observed in populations and cannot be captured by Mendel's binary dominant-recessive model. Epigenetics — the study of heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve changes to the DNA sequence itself — adds a further layer of complexity, demonstrating that the environment can influence which genes are activated across generations. These discoveries do not invalidate Mendel's contributions but expand our understanding of heredity to encompass the full reality of how traits are transmitted and expressed in living organisms.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Pre G4 — Isang Pangarap
text: Lahat tayo ay may pangarap. Si Nena ay may pangarap na maging guro balang araw. Araw-araw, nagtatayo siya ng maliit na paaralan sa ilalim ng puno. Ginagawa niyang mga estudyante ang kanyang mga kapatid at kapitbahay. Nagbibigay siya ng mga takdang-aralin at nagwawasto ng mga papel. Natutuwa ang lahat kapag may klase si Nena. Minsan, tinanong siya ng kanyang ina: 'Bakit gusto mong maging guro?' Sumagot si Nena: 'Gusto kong turuan ang mga bata. Gusto kong matulungan silang matuto ng magbasa at magsulat.' Ngumiti ang ina niya. 'Kung patuloy kang mag-aral at magtrabaho nang husto, maaabot mo ang iyong pangarap,' sabi ng ina. Ngayon, mas pinagsisikapan ni Nena ang kanyang pag-aaral. Alam niya na ang isang pangarap ay nagsisimula sa isang maliit na hakbang.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Pre G5 — Tagtuyot Hatid ng El Nino
text: Bawat ilang taon, nakakaranas ang Pilipinas ng mapaminsalang epekto ng El Nino. Ang El Nino ay isang natural na kaganapan kung saan nagtatag-init ang tubig sa Pasipikong Karagatan, na nagdudulot ng pagbabago sa lagay ng panahon sa buong mundo. Sa Pilipinas, ang El Nino ay kadalasang nagdudulot ng matinding tagtuyot. Nanganganib ang mga pananim ng mga magsasaka dahil sa kakulangan ng ulan. Tumitigas at nagsasabog ang lupa, at namamatay ang maraming halaman. Ang mga ilog at imbakan ng tubig ay nauubos, kaya nagdurusa rin ang mga taong nakatira sa mga probinsya. Sa ilang lugar, naghihirap ang mga pamilya dahil wala silang sapat na pagkain at inuming tubig. Mahalaga ang paghahanda para sa El Nino. Kailangan ng pamahalaan at ng bawat pamilya na mag-imbak ng tubig, magtanim ng mga halaman na matibay sa tagtuyot, at matuto sa mga nakaraang karanasan.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Pre G6 — Ang Puerto Princesa Underground River
text: Ang Puerto Princesa Underground River ay isa sa mga pinaka-kamangha-manghang likas na tagpuan sa buong mundo. Matatagpuan ito sa Palawan, isang probinsya sa kanlurang bahagi ng Pilipinas. Noong 2011, ito ay pinili bilang isa sa New Seven Wonders of Nature. Ang ilog na ito ay umaagos sa loob ng isang yungib na humigit-kumulang 8.2 kilometro ang haba bago umabot sa karagatan. Sa loob ng yungib, makikita ang malalaki at magagandang stalactite at stalagmite na nabuo sa loob ng libu-libong taon. Ang mga taong bumibisita dito ay sinasakay sa mga bangka para makapasok sa yungib. Bukod sa natural na kagandahan nito, ang lugar ay tirahan din ng maraming uri ng hayop, kabilang ang mga ibon, ahas, at palaka. Itinuturing ang Puerto Princesa Underground River na isang mahalagang bahagi ng natural na pamana ng Pilipinas na dapat pangalagaan at protektahan para sa mga susunod na henerasyon.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Pre G7 — Palag Lang
text: Si Mang Tomas ay isang matandang mangingisda na naninirahan sa tabi ng dagat. Sa loob ng maraming taon, inaasahang yumaman siya sa pangingisda, ngunit lagi siyang naibabalik ng hanggang-hinawa sa daungan na may kaunti lamang na nahuli. Isang araw, ang kanyang anak na si Lando ay nagmungkahi: 'Tatay, panahon na para bumili tayo ng bagong lambat. Mas marami tayong mahuhuli.' Tumanggi si Mang Tomas. 'Saan tayo kukuha ng pera para doon?' Ngunit si Lando ay hindi sumuko. Nakiusap siya sa barangay kapitan na tulungan sila sa programa ng pamahalaan para sa mga mangingisda. Nagpursige siya, nagpagal, at sa wakas ay nakakuha ng bagong lambat. Sa unang beses na ginagamit ang bagong lambat, maraming isda ang nahuli. Ngumiti si Mang Tomas at tinapik sa balikat ang kanyang anak. 'Ikaw pala ang dapat kong tularan,' sabi niya. 'Ang palag ay hindi kahulugan ng kabiguan. Ito ay patunay na ikaw ay nagtatangka.'

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Pre G8 — Sino Ka Tao
text: Ang tanong na 'Sino ka?' ay tila madaling sagutin. Ibibigay mo ang iyong pangalan, sasabihin mo kung saan ka nakatira, at ilalista mo ang iyong pamilya at trabaho. Ngunit ang tunay na pagkakakilanlan ng isang tao ay hindi matatagpuan sa mga simpleng katotohanang ito. Ang pagkakakilanlan ay isang masalimuot na konstruksyon na nabubuo sa pamamagitan ng kultura, kasaysayan, karanasan, at relasyon. Para sa isang Pilipino, ang pagkakakilanlan ay lalo pang kumplikado. Tayo ay isang bansang dumaan sa ilang daang taon ng pananakop — una ng Kastila, saka ng mga Amerikano — at ang bawat kolonyal na kapangyarihan ay nag-iwan ng malalim na bakas sa ating wika, relihiyon, at paraan ng pamumuhay. Ngunit ang katotohanan ay mas malalim: ang pagiging Pilipino ay nangangahulugan ng kakayahang isama ang iba't ibang impluwensiya at gawin itong sarili. Ang ating kakayahang mag-angkop, magtiis, at mangarap sa kabila ng lahat ng pagsubok — iyon ang tunay na kahulugan ng pagiging Pilipino.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Pre G9 — Daing ng Kalikasan
text: Kung makapagsasalita ang kalikasan, ano kaya ang kanyang sasabihin? Marahil, magsisimula siya sa isang pagsangit na nangangamoy ng usok at nagtatago sa likod ng mga puting ulap na ginawa ng tao. Marahil, magrereklamo siya ng pag-ulan ng acid rain na kumukuha ng buhay mula sa kanyang mga ilog at lawa. Marahil, makiikilos siya tungkol sa mga kagubatan na nawala — hindi sa mga dekada kundi sa mga taon at kahit buwan lamang. Ang mga palatandaan ng pagbabago ng klima ay lalong malinaw: ang pagtaas ng antas ng dagat, ang pagtindi ng mga bagyo, ang pagkawala ng mga coral reef. Sa kabila nito, maraming tao pa rin ang kumikilos na para bang walang problema. Kailangan nating muling aralin ang ating relasyon sa kalikasan. Hindi tayo ang nagmamay-ari ng kalikasan — tayo ay bahagi nito. Ang pinsala na ating ginagawa sa kalikasan ay pinsala rin sa ating sarili. Ang daing ng kalikasan ay hindi lamang isang metapora — ito ay isang babala na dapat nating pakinggan bago pa huli ang lahat.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Pre G10 — Nang Mauna ang Dapat Mahuli
text: Sa buhay ng tao, mayroong mga sandaling nailalagay sa maling lugar ang mga prioridad. Ang tagumpay sa materyal ay hinahangad nang higit sa pagmamahalan sa pamilya. Ang katanyagan ay hinahabol nang mas masigla kaysa sa integridad. At sa larangan ng pulitika, madalas na ang kapangyarihan ang nauuna kaysa sa serbisyo sa bayan. Ang nobelistang si Jose Rizal, sa pamamagitan ng kanyang mga akda, ay naglalarawan ng ganitong kalagayan — ng mga taong napikot sa mga ilusyon ng kolonyal na kapangyarihan, na naghahanap ng karangalan mula sa mga manananakop sa halip na sa kanilang sariling kultura. Sa kasalukuyang lipunan, patuloy na nangyayari ang ganitong pagpapalit ng priyoridad. Ang mga kabataan ay pinipilit na magtagumpay sa ekonomiya ngunit hindi sila tinuturuan kung paano mabuhay nang may dignidad. Ang edukasyon ay nagiging instrumento ng merkado sa halip na paraan ng pagbuo ng buong tao. Ang hamon sa bawat henerasyon ay ang muling tukuyin kung ano ang dapat mauna at kung ano ang dapat mahuli — at ang lakas ng loob na mamuhay ayon sa mga sagot na iyon, kahit lumalaban ang mundo.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Post G4 — Pahiyas Festival
text: Bawat ika-15 ng Mayo, ipinagdiriwang ng bayan ng Lucban sa Quezon ang Pahiyas Festival. Ito ay isang pista na nagpapasalamat sa maayos na ani ng mga magsasaka. Sa araw na ito, dinidinayuhan ng maraming tao ang Lucban para makita ang magagandang palamuti sa mga bahay. Ang mga pabahay ay nagde-decorate ng kiping, mga gulay, prutas, bulaklak, at iba pang mga produkto mula sa bukid. Ang kiping ay mga kulay-kulay na galamay-atis na yari sa bigas na sinasabit sa mga dingding at bintana ng bahay. Naglalakad ang mga bisita sa mga kalsada at pumipili ng pinakamaganda at pinakamalikhaing palamuti. May mga hurado na pumipili ng pinakamahusay na bahay bawat taon. Malaki ang tuwa ng lahat, lalo na ng mga bata, dahil maraming masasarap na pagkain at sorpresa sa buong bayan. Ang Pahiyas Festival ay isang pagdiriwang ng sining, kultura, at pasasalamat ng mga taga-Lucban sa kanilang kabuhayan.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Post G5 — Kapaligiran
text: Ang kapaligiran ay ang ating tahanan. Dito tayo nabubuhay, kumakain, at lumalago. Ang malinis na kapaligiran ay nagbibigay sa atin ng sariwang hangin, malinis na tubig, at masustansyang pagkain. Ngunit sa kasalukuyan, maraming bahagi ng ating kapaligiran ang nasisirang dahil sa mga gawa ng tao. Ang mga pabrika ay nagtatapon ng usok sa hangin. Ang mga basura ay itinitapon sa mga ilog at karagatan. Ang mga gubat ay pinipintasan para sa lupaing maaaring itayo ng mga gusali o sakahan. Dahil dito, maraming halaman at hayop ang nanganganib. Mabilis na nagbabago ang klima, at naghihirap ang maraming tao sa mga baha, tagtuyot, at matinding bagyo. Ang bawat isa sa atin ay may responsibilidad sa pangangalaga ng kapaligiran. Maaari tayong mag-ulit ng basura, gumamit ng mas kaunting kuryente, at magtanim ng mga puno. Ang maliliit na hakbang ng bawat isa ay maaaring makagawa ng malaking pagbabago para sa ating kalikasan.

label: Literal
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Post G6 — Populasyon
text: Ang populasyon ng Pilipinas ay patuloy na lumalaki. Ayon sa pinakabagong datos, mahigit 110 milyong Pilipino na ang nakatira sa ating bansa. Ito ay nagdudulot ng maraming hamon para sa pamahalaan at sa bawat komunidad. Kabilang sa mga hamon ang pagbibigay ng sapat na pagkain, pabahay, paaralan, at trabaho sa lahat ng mamamayan. Sa mga lungsod tulad ng Maynila at Cebu, mabilis na lumalaki ang populasyon dahil maraming tao ang lumilipat mula sa probinsya para maghanap ng trabaho. Dahil dito, nagiging masikip at nagiging mahirap ang pamumuhay sa mga lungsod. Sa kabukiran naman, mababa ang populasyon ngunit kulang ang mga serbisyo ng pamahalaan. Mahalaga ang family planning o responsableng pagpaplano ng pamilya para matulungan ang mga pamilya na mapamahalaan ang laki ng kanilang pamilya. Kapag ang populasyon ay maayos na napamamahalaan, mas madaling maiangat ng bansa ang kalidad ng buhay ng bawat mamamayan.

label: Inferential
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Post G7 — Mahalin Natin ang Ating Kapaligiran
text: Ang kalikasan ay hindi lamang isang background sa ating buhay — ito ay pundasyon ng lahat ng ating ginagawa. Kung wala ang malinis na hangin, tubig, at lupa, walang sibilisasyon ang makakatagal. Sa kabila nito, patuloy tayong nakikita na nananakit sa kalikasan: nagtatambak ng basura sa mga ilog, nagputuputol ng mga punong hindi kailangang putulin, at gumagamit ng mga plastik kahit alam natin ang pinsalang dulot nito. Minsan, ang problema ay tila napakalaki at napakahirap na solusyunan kaya pakiramdam natin ay walang silbi ang ating gagawin. Ngunit ang katotohanan ay bawat maliit na kilos ay may kahulugan. Kung bawat Pilipino ay magtatanim ng isang puno sa kanyang buhay, isipa mo kung gaano karaming puno ang maidadagdag sa ating kapaligiran. Ang pagmamahal sa kapaligiran ay hindi isang opsyon — ito ay isang pananagutan. At ang pagtupad sa pananagutang iyon ay nagsisimula sa bawat isa sa atin, dito at ngayon.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Post G8 — Pangunahing Senyales ng Diabetes sa mga Bata
text: Ang diabetes ay isang sakit na patuloy na nagpapalakas sa buong mundo, at hindi na ito eksklusibo sa mga matatanda. Sa nakalipas na ilang dekada, ang bilang ng mga bata at kabataang nagkakaroon ng Type 2 diabetes ay kapansin-pansing tumaas. Ang sakit na ito ay nangyayari kapag hindi na sapat ang produksyon ng insulin ng katawan o hindi na epektibo ang paggamit nito, na nagreresulta sa mataas na antas ng glucose sa dugo. Ang mga pangunahing palatandaan ng diabetes sa mga bata ay kinabibilangan ng madalas na pag-ihi, matinding pagkauhaw, biglaang pagbaba ng timbang sa kabila ng normal na pagkain, paulit-ulit na puyat, at mabagal na paggaling ng mga sugat. Ang ilan ay nagrereklamo rin ng malabong paningin at pamamanhid ng mga kamay at paa. Kung hindi agad matutugunan, ang diabetes ay maaaring humantong sa seryosong komplikasyon tulad ng sakit sa puso, kidney failure, at pagkabulag. Mahalaga ang maagang pagtukoy at tamang pamamahala ng sakit sa pamamagitan ng wastong diyeta, regular na ehersisyo, at medikal na gabay.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Post G9 — Alegorya ng Upuan
text: Ang upuan ay isang simpleng bagay. Ito ay ginawa para umupo ang tao — para magpahinga, para manilbihan sa iba. Ngunit sa ating lipunan, ang upuan ay naging simbolo ng kapangyarihan. Ang upuang pinakamataas ay hinahangad ng lahat, ngunit hindi lahat ay karapat-dapat dito. Maraming umaangat sa kapangyarihan hindi dahil sa kanilang kakayahan o integridad, kundi dahil sa kanilang koneksyon, kayamanan, o kakayahang dayain ang sistema. Kapag umupo na sila, nakalimutan na nila kung bakit sila umupo — kung para saan ang kanilang posisyon. Ginagamit nila ang upuan para sa sarili nilang kapakanan, hindi para sa mga taong dapat nilang pagsilbihan. Ang alegoryang ito ay hindi kailanman nawala sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas. Mula sa panahon ng kolonyal na pamumuno hanggang sa kasalukuyang demokrasya, paulit-ulit na ang kwentong ito. Ang tanong na dapat nating itanong ay hindi lamang kung sino ang umupo kundi para kaninong kapakanan ang upuang iyon. Hanggang hindi natin sinasagot ang tanong na ito nang buong katapatan, hindi tayo makalalabas sa bilog ng kapangyarihang walang pananagutan.

label: Evaluative
name: Phil-IRI 2024 JHS FIL Post G10 — Whang-Od
text: Sa nayon ng Buscalan sa Kalinga, Pilipinas, naninirahan ang isang babae na itinuring ng marami bilang isa sa mga pinakamahalagang tagapag-ingat ng katutubong kultura ng bansa. Si Whang-Od Oggay, ipinanganak noong 1917, ay ang pinakatanda at pinakakilalang mambabatok — isang manggagawa ng tradisyunal na Kalinga na pagtatato. Sa loob ng mahigit isang siglo, ginagamit niya ang isang tinik ng pomelo at karbong tubig na nakalagay sa isang maliit na kawayan upang mantatao ng mga makabuluhang simbolo sa balat ng mga nagnanais ng batok. Ang mga disenyo na kanyang ginagawa ay higit sa ornamentation: ang bawat linya ay may kahulugang kultural at espirituwal, nagtatala ng katayuan ng isang tao sa komunidad, ng kanyang mga tagumpay, at ng kanyang koneksyon sa kanyang mga ninuno. Sa pamamagitan ng kanyang gawain, nagpapatuloy si Whang-Od ng isang tradisyon na maaaring mawala. Nakilala siya ng pamahalaan ng Pilipinas bilang isang Gawad sa Manlilikha ng Bayan, ang pinakamataas na parangal na ibinibigay sa mga katutubong artisano. Ang kanyang kwento ay nagpapaalaala sa atin na ang tunay na sining ay hindi lamang ganda — ito ay pagpapatuloy ng pagkakakilanlan, kahulugan, at pag-alaala.
